asDecan.p: Your Sun is somewhere between 10 and 19 degrees of Virgo, and in the Chaldean order Venus rules those ten degrees. Every sign is split into three of these slices, called decans, each with its own planet and its own numbered card, and the middle one is where the sign has settled in and is at full strength. It's an awkward match, to be honest. Venus is in fall in Virgo, which means she's uncomfortable there and doesn't get much of a hearing, so the part of you that wants pleasure and nice things has to come in by a side door, usually by way of something done properly. The slices either side of yours feel quite different. The Eight, the Sun's, is still at the bench learning the trade. The Ten, Mercury's, is working out what gets left to whom. Yours has done the work and would like to enjoy it. The Hermit, Virgo's Major, is your Sun card, and this is the smaller card that belongs to your particular degrees.

You can tell from one sip whether a new café is worth going back to, and if it isn't, you just quietly never go back. A Sunday with nothing planned is one of your favourite things, as long as the flat's been tidied first, and it usually means a long walk, the market, a good loaf of bread and nobody asking where you are. At a family dinner you're the one who notices the tablecloth's been ironed and says so, and notices the gravy came out of a packet and keeps that to yourself. Mercury rules Virgo, so there's a running commentary in your head about how most things could be done a bit better, and enjoyment has to get past it before you'll let yourself have any. When it does, the bath at the right temperature, the book good, the phone in another room, you're about as content as anyone I know.

You can make not much money feel like plenty. Venus works sideways in Virgo, through care and editing, and you've learned to get real pleasure from a few good things chosen slowly. Your first flat was probably nicer than friends' places that cost twice as much, and guests still notice it at yours. There's a towel folded on the end of the bed, a glass of water beside it, decent soap in the bathroom, and nobody saw you do any of it. It reaches past your own front door, too. When a friend moves out after a break-up with a suitcase and not much else, you're the one who turns up with three plates, a lamp, a proper knife and a pot plant, and you don't leave until the bed's made up.

You find it hard to enjoy anything you didn't earn. A friend pays for dinner and you spend dessert working out how to pay them back, probably with interest. Someone gives you a spa voucher for your birthday and it sits in a drawer for eleven months, because a whole afternoon of being looked after, with nothing to show for it at the end, feels faintly wrong. Pleasure only gets let in once it's been paid for with effort, and a gift hasn't been. There's a sharper edge as well, and you probably know about it. You can be a bit snobbish about other people's comforts, the takeaway, the reality telly, the cask wine, the matching lounge suite, and people pick up on the little pause before you tell them it all looks lovely.

In a bad stretch, a job that ends badly, a death in the family, months of being passed over at work, your first move is often to buy one very good thing. A heavy pan, a wool jumper, proper sheets. It's a private way of telling yourself life is still under control, and it comes with a lot of tidying, the drawers sorted, the car cleaned. From outside you look fine. About a week later the Virgo side turns on you, and you're going back over every decision, fairly sure you should have seen it coming. You pull back from people and tell them you're fine, you just need a bit of time at home. The ones who are usually welcome in that home feel locked out, and it hurts them more than you'd guess. What helps is letting one person in while the place is a mess, and saying yes when they offer to take you out, even somewhere you wouldn't have picked.

For someone so good on their own, you want to be courted more than people would guess, and properly. A real restaurant, a day somebody else has planned, flowers that didn't come from the petrol station. You'd never ask for any of it, and when the effort isn't there you notice, even if you don't say a word. You're slow to choose anyone and you'd sooner be single than settle, which can read as cool from outside. Once you're in, a lot of your love comes out as quiet fixes. You'll sew the button back on their coat without mentioning it, and you know which cheese they like and which wine gives them a headache. With Venus in fall, the soft thing said out loud is harder, and a partner who needs a lot of words can end up unsure of you. Tell them what you'd like, plainly, a good week before your birthday.

You're the person whose finished work looks easy, and nobody sees the eleven drafts. This slice wants the work to pay for a life you actually like, so you tend to end up self-employed, or senior enough to set your own hours, or somewhere taste is the product, editing, interiors, a small restaurant, garden design, a skin clinic, fine furniture. You're good with money in a quiet way, and you rarely carry debt. Where it costs you is pricing. Venus is the planet of what things are worth, and with her in fall it's hard to put a proper value on your own work, so you undercharge for years, then get resentful and blame the clients. Colleagues who charge double for half the care drive you up the wall. Put your rates up every year, or ask for the raise, whether or not you feel ready.

Early on there's usually a gap between your taste and your bank balance. You want the good coffee and the linen shirt on a first-job wage, and you can feel almost apologetic about it when friends seem happy with whatever's going. A lot of people with this decan work very hard in their twenties and don't enjoy much of it. By the mid-thirties it tends to come together, a place of your own set up exactly how you like it, some savings, a routine that suits, and the independence people admire in you is real by then. That's often when you notice you've built the whole garden and haven't asked anyone round to see it. The fifties usually soften things. People in this slice tend to get better at being given things, travel more, spend on pleasure without the long justification, and let their friends see how much they matter.

Each month, set aside a small fixed amount, say thirty dollars, for something purely for pleasure, with one rule. It can't be useful. No tools, no kitchen gear, no books you'll learn something from. A bunch of flowers, a very good peach, a ticket to a gig. Use it the same day, on your own if you like, and when the Virgo voice starts listing what the money could have gone on, let it finish the list and keep eating the peach.
